newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico bellwhether primary Cetes rate seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Mexico bellwhether primary Cetes rate seen rising.

text.p: The interest rate on the bellwhether one-month Cetes will show a small increase at the primary Treasury bill auction on Tuesday, rising on expectations of a rebound in inflation in the last quarter of the year, analysts said.
"They (rates) will have to respond to inflationary pressures. The secondary market has been relatively quiet, but if rates drop some more the paper will be less competitive," said one market analyst.
A survey of Mexico City brokerage houses by Reuters forecast average inflation of 1.66 percent in September, after the 1.33 percent rise in August.
One analyst said that an increase in the inflation rate of 1.6 percent in September would leave the real return on the 28-day paper at around three percent.
During the last primary auction, the 28-day rate fell 10 basis points to 23.28 percent, a level considered the short-term floor.
In the 182-day and one-year terms, analysts said that high real returns and expectations of lower long-term inflation give room for these rates to decline.
A decline in the 182-day and one-year paper rates below their secondary market levels supports the forecasts of mixed movements in the primary auction, analysts said.
Banco de Mexico will offer 3.3 billion worth of Cetes in the auction this week.
